seo.title: Krillion Answers for October 20, 2026 | Dive #97
seo.description: Explore Krillion answers for October 20, 2026, Dive #97, with seven daily questions, recorded scores, rarity tiers, and answer lists for every round.

questions.prompt: Name something sold in stick form (like deodorant)

answers.note: A miswak is a natural tooth-cleaning twig, so the object itself is sold and used in stick form.

questions.hint: Think beyond toiletries: foods, craft materials, cosmetics, and traditional tools can all be sold as sticks.
questions.explanation: Miswak and spurtle reached the 100-point tier in this revealed set. Deodorant fits, but the example in the prompt makes it an obvious low-scoring choice.
questions.watchFor: The answer must commonly be sold as a stick, not merely be long or stick-shaped after it is prepared.

questions.prompt: Name a food made by mashing or puréeing (like guacamole)

answers.note: Moretum is an ancient Roman herb-and-cheese spread prepared by grinding its ingredients together.

questions.hint: Look across dips, fruit preparations, vegetable dishes, and regional foods produced by pounding, mashing, or blending.
questions.explanation: The accepted pool is very large. A familiar answer is safer to spell, while regional preparations create more high-scoring possibilities.
questions.watchFor: Choose a finished food whose preparation genuinely involves mashing or puréeing; a dish merely served with a mashed ingredient may not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a country with the letter D in its name (like Canada)

answers.note: The conjunction “and” supplies the required letter while the full sovereign-state name remains a clean match.

questions.hint: Check the complete English country name. Multi-word Caribbean and Pacific states offer less obvious choices.
questions.explanation: There are only 50 recorded answers for this prompt, so the category boundary is much tighter than the food or mammal rounds.
questions.watchFor: Use a country rather than a city, territory, dependency, continent, or historical state, and enter the standard English name.

questions.prompt: Name a device that blows air

answers.note: A winnowing machine uses a directed airflow to separate lighter chaff from grain.

questions.hint: Consider household appliances, industrial machinery, entertainment equipment, and devices used to move or direct air.
questions.explanation: Fan and hair dryer are easy fallbacks, but the revealed list rewards specialized equipment much more heavily.
questions.watchFor: The named object should function as a device and actively expel or direct air, rather than merely contain air or move because of wind.

questions.prompt: Name a mammal smaller than a house cat

answers.note: The hero shrew is a small Central African mammal known for its unusually reinforced spine.

questions.hint: Small bats, rodents, shrews, mustelids, and compact marsupials offer many possible answers. Check the typical adult size.
questions.explanation: With 6,514 recorded answers, this round offers the most room to trade familiarity for rarity without leaving the category.
questions.watchFor: Use a mammal whose typical adult size is below that of a domestic cat; baby forms of normally larger species are weak choices.

answers.note: The World began offering dial-up internet access to the public from Brookline, Massachusetts, in 1989.

questions.hint: Recall regional broadband companies, former dial-up brands, mobile carriers, and providers outside your home country.
questions.explanation: This is the day’s largest pool. Regional and discontinued providers dominate the higher tiers, while major national brands remain reliable low-tier answers.
questions.watchFor: Name a company that actually provides internet access, not a search engine, browser, website, router brand, or streaming service.

questions.prompt: Name something that has a saddle

answers.note: The dandy horse was an early two-wheeled running machine with a saddle but no pedals.

questions.hint: A saddle may be a seat, a structural shape, a named body feature, or a component on an instrument or machine.
questions.explanation: Earthworm is accepted because its clitellum is commonly called a saddle. That broader meaning is what makes the final round less obvious than it first appears.
questions.watchFor: The connection must use the word saddle in a recognized sense. A vague resemblance to a seat or curve is not enough.
